target_customer: Brand and agency social media marketers who manage large Facebook Pages
problem: Facebook's own Insights gave brands shallow data on how many fans a post actually reached. Marketers wanted deeper post level analytics to judge content and ad spend.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for Facebook Page analytics, with a free tool (Minilytics) as a lead generator

founders.name: Jeff Widman
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch described him as a former TechCrunch intern. YC page says he started and sold two companies and can move between marketer and engineer roles.

founders.name: David Turner
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page as a former founder. Named as co-founder in TechCrunch coverage of the acquisition.

competitors.name: Wildfire
competitors.what: Social marketing and Facebook campaign and analytics platform

competitors.name: Involver
competitors.what: Social marketing platform for Facebook pages and apps

competitors.name: Facebook Insights
competitors.what: Facebook's free built in Page analytics
competitors.traction_then: default tool for all Page admins

technical_complexity.rationale: Pulled data from the Facebook Graph API and Insights and re-presented it with deeper reach metrics. Standard data pipeline and dashboard work for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Built entirely on data Facebook exposed, with several funded competitors and the risk that Facebook would ship the same metrics itself. Little switching cost beyond historical data.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Facebook was named in 2011 coverage as a possible competitor via Insights. The company was bought by the social ads startup Unified in January 2013 and folded into its platform.

market_need_then: Brands were pouring budget into Facebook Pages in 2011 and found Facebook's own Insights too thin. The launch coverage cited YouTube, Mint and Kayak.com as early customers, and the YC page says four of the top 10 Facebook pages used it.

identity.voice_and_tone: Product press used phrases like Facebook Insights on steroids

rebrands.why: Original tool was renamed when the real time PageLever Now product launched, per search summary of press

branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage at launch and for new releases (TechCrunch, Adweek, The Next Web). No evidence of merch or fan community.

brand_strength.rationale: Trade press coverage but no sourced evidence of a distinct identity beyond the product name; the brand disappeared into Unified after 2013.

outcome_analysis: PageLever rode the 2011 rush of brands onto Facebook Pages and gained notable customers, but it depended on Facebook's data and faced funded competitors. It sold to Unified in January 2013 with seven employees joining, a small exit consistent with a thin moat and no disclosed venture rounds beyond the YC seed.
notes: Company website returned HTTP 503 at fetch time. Seedtable lists an August 2011 seed with Y Combinator, Start Fund and SV Angel but no amount; only one aggregator, so unverified and not recorded as a round. Education and prior employers not found in opened sources. Competitors search for dated 2011 results returned only modern pages; competitors come from the August 2011 TechCrunch article. Completeness pass: the August 2011 seed is now recorded as a round (no amount given) and rests on Seedtable, with an Adweek launch article reporting the same SV Angel and Start Fund backing without an amount. Cross-check searches found no amount. Unified Social acquired the company in January 2013.
